sources.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
sources.authority_reason: Authors’ original empirical study of model size, seen training tokens, fixed-compute loss allocation and its stated limitations.
sources.inspection_note: Read original PDF text with pdftotext -layout. Model/token allocation is an empirical question under a chosen compute constraint; over 400 runs and multiple training horizons underlie the fitted laws. Its infinite-data/subepoch condition differs from the repeated tiny corpus. Appendix F supplies 2-FLOP multiply-accumulate convention and separate dense/attention contributions. Actual reading: Abstract and §1, Eq. (1), footnote 2; §3 opening and §3.3 Eq. (2); §5 Discussion & Conclusion limitations, PDF pp. 15–16; Appendix F, PDF pp. 27–28. Receipt a_sources contains original fingerprints and necessary short excerpts.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook §5.3.3.3 Full factorial designs
sources.authority_reason: Official NIST statistical engineering handbook defines a two-factor/two-level full factorial design.
sources.inspection_note: Read the full short official page. It explicitly lists two factors at two levels as four runs. Supports the four-cell controlled comparison, not a universal prediction of quality. Actual reading: §5.3.3.3 full factorial designs in two levels and Table 3.2. Receipt a_sources contains original fingerprints and necessary short excerpts.

Actual reading: Linear docstring, weight shape and __init__/forward, lines 53–140. Receipt a_sources contains original fingerprints and necessary short excerpts.

With unweighted integer labels and no smoothing, summing losses then dividing by nonignored count gives mean NLL. sources.title: Transparent budget, parameter and FLOP derivations
sources.details: Fixed plan: 4 records/update ×8 targets/record ×100 updates =3200 target exposures; 400 record draws correspond to average25 draws/record at16 records and6.25 at64, without asserting each record is equally sampled. Exercise3200/(4×4)=200 and4×4×100=1600. For defaults vocab264, max_length128, one untied block: input embedding264w + position128w + output264w + final LN2w =658w; block has attention4w² + FFN8w²+5w + two LayerNorms4w =12w²+9w. Total P(w)=12w²+667w, giving6104,13744,33632 for w8,16,32. A dense D→M transform uses DM multiplies and M(D−1) additions in a minimal dot-product summation, conventionally approximated as2DM FLOPs, with bias and lower-order terms omitted. Therefore8→8≈128 and16→16≈512, a4× increase for that square Linear; not a4× claim about the entire model. A mean over distinct target sets is not a score on one common new set. The actual training post-update means cover553 targets for16 records and2200 for64; shared validation274 and test276 are separately fixed.

limitations.details: Plan values are labeled untrained assumptions. Fixed steps, supervision, FLOPs and seconds are distinguished;2DM is an approximation for one dense layer. Train-set means do not represent a common new set. One seed,four synthetic settings and repeated data cannot establish large-model scaling laws. Public inference export omits training state; original settings come from recorded result and unchanged relevant code, while CPU diagnostic rechecks weights/metrics without retraining.
